title: Parse stored numeric text inside a SQL query
goal: Parse numeric text in SQL Server filters with EF11 single-string Parse translations, choosing deliberate SQL conversion and failure semantics.

selectionNotes: Osprey survey imports store numeric text. EF11 translates the single-string byte, short, int, long, decimal, float and double Parse calls to tinyint, smallint, int, bigint, decimal(18,2), real and float CAST expressions. The executed filter returns only reading 1. Invalid text, int overflow and comma-decimal text fail at SQL Server with conversion errors; no TryParse guarantee is implied. A nullable result projection propagates SQL NULL. CLR Parse(null) instead throws; culture-sensitive CLR parsing is not the SQL grammar. The French CLR control accepts 1,5 as 1.5 while the integer SQL cast rejects it. Decimal CAST has fixed scale and can round differently from CLR decimal.Parse. No culture/provider overload or arbitrary .NET numeric format is promised. EF10 rejects Parse in a predicate; its fixed SQL TRY_CAST alternative treats failed conversions as NULL and excludes them. TRY_CAST deliberately has different error semantics from CAST. A WHERE guard is not a guarantee of SQL expression evaluation order. Clean input before conversion or use a deliberate TRY_CAST policy.

title: Store half-precision values in SQLite
goal: Persist nullable Half measurements through SQLite parameters and EF11 mapping, preserving explicit precision and REAL storage boundaries.

selectionNotes: Osprey gauges measure finite half-precision values. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite11 binds boxed Half and GetFieldValue<Half> reads it; EF11 maps nullable Half directly. EF10 uses an explicit double parameter/read cast and an explicit expression converter. The generic HasConversion<double>() call alone does not supply this older Half converter. Actual zero, rounded 1.1, extrema, minimum subnormal and NULL round-trip; a fresh EF context reads the same nullable values. SQLite stores non-null parameters as REAL and nulls as NULL. Half is a 16-bit CLR type, not a promise of two-byte SQLite disk storage. Precision is already lost when converting 1.1 to Half; REAL cannot recover it. Reading 100000.0 into Half overflows to positive infinity, so validate the finite range before accepting wider values. This example teaches finite scalar columns only. JSON mapping, NaN payload preservation, signed-zero bit identity and encryption are not established by these checks and are not taught as supported routes.

title: Preserve queued request capacity when replacing retired middleware
goal: Replace ConcurrencyLimiter middleware with a global concurrency rate limiter while preserving capacity, queue order and rejection behavior under saturation.

selectionNotes: The retired middleware source has been removed and no new Microsoft.AspNetCore.ConcurrencyLimiter 11.x package ships. An older package may be retained temporarily; this recipe verifies it only on net10.0, not a net11.0 retained-package route. The replacement is shared-framework middleware with one global partition, PermitLimit=1, QueueLimit=1, OldestFirst and explicit 503 rejection to preserve the historical behavior. A concurrency limiter bounds simultaneous executions, not requests per time interval. Limits are per process, not distributed; no Retry-After estimate is available from concurrency alone.

title: Choose response compression and accepted request encodings
goal: Offer Zstandard with a gzip fallback and limit accepted compressed uploads when clients support different content encodings.

selectionNotes: Explicit response providers replace automatic defaults: zstd and gzip only here. Explicitly remove br/deflate from the built-in request decoder registry; unsupported or stacked encodings normally pass through the middleware, so this app returns 415 when Content-Encoding remains. Response negotiation and request decoding are independent. HTTPS compression stays disabled because reflected secrets can leak through compressed size. Limit decompressed bodies as well as wire bytes. Built-in Zstandard needs .NET 11; no external .NET 10 codec route is verified. Browser/WASI are unsupported by the built-in codec.
